commit message:
These edits are to overcome cmake warnings of the form:
"install Library TARGETS given no DESTINATION!"

cmake (> v2.6) documentation (e.g. http://www.cmake.org/cmake/help/cmake2.6docs.html#command:install) states:
"For DLL platforms the DLL part of a shared library is treated as a RUNTIME target and the corresponding import library is treated as an ARCHIVE target. All Windows-based systems including Cygwin are DLL platforms. The ARCHIVE, LIBRARY, RUNTIME, and FRAMEWORK arguments change the type of target to which the subsequent properties apply. If none is given the installation properties apply to all target types. If only one is given then only targets of that type will be installed (which can be used to install just a DLL or just an import library)."

This implies that we either need to add install rules for ARCHIVE targets as well or simply delete the LIBRARY from the current install rule (so that install properties apply to "all" target types). An alternative explanation is at: http://www.cmake.org/pipermail/cmake/2008-September/023876.html

commit message:
Move OctomapOcTree::checkStandable to SpaceMapUtil

We should keep the calculation on Octomap away from OctomapOcTree, or
the OctomapOcTree class will be too fat. Now all of the calculation
functions are put in the SpaceMapUtil.

Note that I remove the

if (pos.z < mfloorHeight) {
    return false;
}

check in checkStandable. Because In most of the use cases we don't know
the height of the floor. This variable seems useful in old embodiment in
Unity 3D game world, but it looks confusing in real world. Also, if the
position is really out of so-called border in z coordinate, there will be
no block under it, so the checkStandable still returns false correctly.

This change cause some problems: we have to explictly pass the
AtomSpace argument in checkStandable and getNearFreePoint
calculation utilities now because after we move checkStandable
function out, the OctomapOcTree is 100% not related to AtomSpace.
But that will make parameter list looks too long. Also, for now we
put the agentHeight member in OctomapOcTree, but obviously it's also
not used in the OctomapOcTree after moving checkStandable. So, we now
have to consider where to put agentHeight variable.

One obvious way, I think, is to make SpaceMapUtil become a class, responsible
for doing calculation. So we can put AtomSpace and SpaceMap which are heavily
used in calculation in SpaceMapUtil to reduce parameters. Also we can put
required info(ex. agentHeight) there. This seems a correct direction to seperate
Octomap data structure and all the calculation on Octomap.

commit message:
Change way redundant features are removed for inc algo

Before when given a redundent set of feature the algorithm would go
through each one, remove it temporarily to see if it decrease the
feature score move than threshold, put it back if it doesn't let it
removed if it does. The problem is that when presented with several
options it would remove the features that are presented first rather
than the worst ones. Now it tries all possibilities and remove the
worst. It probably more costly but it makes more sense and when the
number of interaction terms is 1 (the typical use case) it's probably
about the same.

commit message:
Fix operator>>() craziness.

combo/vertex.h failed to instantiate operator>>() for the combo tree,
which resulted in compile errors that were worked around in util/tree.h
by placing the tree operator>> into the std namespace, instead of the
opencog namespace. This in turn broke moses, which worked around it by
instantiating operator>> in a santa-fe-trail ant file, resulting in the
ant header files being included in a bunch of combo code.

This changeset puts operator>> back into the correct namespaces, and it
instantiates it for the vertex, and the combo_tree. Everything now
compiles, and all unit tests pass.

Changed OPENCOG_ADD_ATOM_TYPES macro so that it generates code for opencog/atomspace library differently from other libraries that adds atom types. That's because opencog/atomspace/atom_types.inheritance is included inside ClassServer constructor and so, it should not call opencog::classserver() there. Otherwise it gets infinite recursivity.
A few definitions of Embodiment-related atom types were moved from opencog/atomspace to opencog/embodiment/AtomSpaceExtensions already. The remaining module-specific atom types should be moved to their specific folders as well, after careful analysis and tests.

commit message:
Work in progress. Fix for https://github.com/opencog/opencog/issues/1240

I've traced it to memory leaks in embodiement operational avatar
controller. E.g. PsiActionSelectionAgent::executeAction() allocates
"SchemeEval* evaluator = new SchemeEval(&atomSpace);" but there is no
corresponding delete. Repeated calls were opening pipes, and they were
not being closed because the object wasn't being destroyed. Eventually
giving the 'too many files open' error.

I'm chainging the code to remove pointers for the local creation of an
evaluator. This should help remove any further problems like this in the
future. E.g. SchemeEval evaluator1(&atomSpace);

It appears to work. Just let me tidy it up and I'll submit a pull
request.

commit message:
Replace usage of the deprecated SGI STL extensions (ext/hash*) with the
semi-official TR1 ones (tr1/unordered*). This silences a huge number of
deprecation warnings on GCC 4.3+ and prepares the tree for future compiler
revisions. However, this will probably render opencog unbuildable if using
not-too-old compilers (it apears that at least GCC 3.X will break but I
haven't been able to confirm this).

author: chenesan <pipio1994@gmail.com>
commit message:
Move OctomapOcTree::checkStandable to SpaceMapUtil

We should keep the calculation on Octomap away from OctomapOcTree, or
the OctomapOcTree class will be too fat. Now all of the calculation
functions are put in the SpaceMapUtil.

But this change cause some problems: we have to explictly pass the
AtomSpace argument in checkStandable and getNearFreePoint
calculation utilities now because after we move checkStandable
function out, the OctomapOcTree is 100% not related to AtomSpace.
But that will make parameter list looks too long. Also, for now we
put the agentHeight member in OctomapOcTree, but obviously it's also
not used in the OctomapOcTree after moving checkStandable. So, we now
have to consider where to put agentHeight variable.

One obvious way, I think, is to make SpaceMapUtil become a class, responsible
for doing calculation. So we can put AtomSpace and SpaceMap which are heavily
used in calculation in SpaceMapUtil to reduce parameters. Also we can put
required info(ex. agentHeight) there. This seems a correct direction to seperate
Octomap data structure and all the calculation on Octomap.

commit message:
Argh. Fuck you too, boost::asio

Surely pthread cancellation is the worst possible solution
to the problem of halting a thread blocked on a socket, but
there appears to be no other way of accomplishing this with
the current boost::asio interfaces. My gut impression is that
boost::asio is mis-designed -- everything that it does, it does
wrong.

We never should have used boost to begin with. The standard unix
socket API is easier to use, simpler to understand and manipulate,
compared to the over-complexticated boost::asio interfaces.  Why
did we use something big, complex, deficient and buggy, when a
simpler alternative existed?  I dunno.

commit message:
Bug fix for  https://bugs.launchpad.net/opencog/+bug/973023

Applied patch from Aleksandar Kodzhabashev:


The first bug is in Plane::TransformSelf and is described in Bug
#973023. The method fails a unit test with the identity map when it is
supposed to return the same plane(normal, distanceFromOrigo) but instead
returns a plane(normal, - distanceFromOrigo). The fix is to multiply the
transformation matrix with the Vector4 formed from the normal of the
plane and (!) - distanceFromOrigo instead, which is the same as the one
given by the Plane::getVector4.

The second bug is in Plane::getIntersectionPoint and is that the
intersection point found by the method has all it's coordinates with
opposite signs. The fix is to take the negative of the vector formed
from the distanceFromOrigo fields of the three planes when doing the
calculation. 

Both these bugs are due to the strange behaviour of the constructors of
Plane and the Plane::set method to assign the distanceFromOrigo field of
the plane to the negative of the distance to the origin. I can see that
the other methods compensate for that in their own ways, but probably
someone forgot to change it in the two methods I fixed.

The bug in Vector3::operator== is failing on a unit test for Plane which
uses Vector3 equality (this is the last unit test for Plane). This is
due simply not taking into account floating point errors, so I
introduced an epsilon=1e-06 to the comparison.

After fixing these 3 bugs my unit tests for the Plane class pass
successfully.

random number generator. This requires passing these two args through

It would be nice if there was some way of wrapping up calls in C++

any easy way...

commit message:
moses: create a top-level moses algorithm class.

The last 27 or so commits, over the last 2-3 days, were leading up to
this.  I needed a way to run moses, and then get at the metapopulation,
after it was done running. Unfortunately, the original code structure
nested the metapop two levels deep inside of template functions.  (To
see this nesting, just consider the location of the print_metapop()
function, and what it would take to pull it out.).

Unwrapping the nesting had several ugly side-effects: a much heavier
use of base classes, difficulties with object lifetimes, and the 
elimination of much of the template code.   The difficulties with
object lifetimes caused a much greater use of new/delete than I'd like.

Hmm... I think there may be a better way to do all this... 
How does bzr branch work again?

commit message:
add optimized version of loadTable and loadITable

add loadTable_optimized and loadITable_optimized, those versions
discard features directly instead of loading them and then removing
them. On large datasets (70K rows and 1K features) the loading time is
sped up by at least 2x when ignoring about 9/10 of the features.

However, it is not working for sparse datasets, and it assumes that
there is a header. Since I wasn't sure it would really speed things up
I didn't care to do things the proper way. Now I know it does speed
things up so I think we should reimplement all the load and istream
functions to ignore features head-on like those optimizations do, the
proper way this time (dealing in the case without header and sparse
data).

Show a limitation, if the variable is constructed with Variable then
the same variable can be used by operators of different types without
raising an error. Basically the type checker is unable to bind the
and remember the type of a variable.

This can be worked around by introducing other variable constructors
like ConceptVariable, PredicateVariable and TVVariable, but it's not
very elegant.

commit message:
- Added SpaceServer as a member of AtomSpace. 
 - In order to SpaceServer do not reference AtomSpace cyclicly, a SpaceServerContainer abstract class was created. AtomSpace now extends it. 
 - Changed references to both AtomSpace and SpaceServer through the whole codebase (mainly under embodiment) properly
 - Resolved unbiguities between ::_1 (used by boost::bind) and std::tr1::placeholders::_1 (used by std::bind). These ambiguities started happening after including SpaceServer.h in AtomSpace.h, what made all headers from opencog/spatial be included there as well. 
 - Resolved conflict with #define clauses in opencog/atomspace/Foreach.h and opencog/util/foreach.h. Both of them were defining OPENCOG_FOREACH_H, which caused annoying compiler errors in the sequence of headers. Now we have OPENCOG_UTIL_FOREACH_H and OPENCOG_ATOMSPACE_FOREACH_H

3) The contin MI scorer does not support interaction terms > 1

the number of candidate selected inside the function select_candidates
but that function if used in a multi_threaded env this would
result in an non-determinism with the candidate being selected (very annoying to debug).
Instead I put the cap on the deme, non more undeterminism
but one may need to set it higher because it now includes
redundant candidates in that number

that way if the scorer implements it, it may speed-up evaluation

Merged staging revision 2185: 
  Implement Boris' idea that Handle uuid's should be stored with the atom
  itself.  This seems to be an all-around win, with no down-side.  This 
  removes the need for an rb-tree map to hold these values (thus reducing 
  memory usage), and it eliminates the need to perform lookups in this
  map, thus reducing CPU usage. Total complexity is lower, seems like a
  win to me. 
  
  This patch stops short of inventing a new API; the existing TLB API
  is re-used.

commit message:
Fix PatternMatch::do_match so that EinstenUTest passes

The problem was that PMCGroundings only grounds the matches after
their all discovered, the so the negative clause

(NotLink
    (clause PN "IsSamePerson" VN "$person_a" VN "$person_b")
)

could not apply.

I've re-added back the simple case of calling directly
PatternMatchEngine::match with the initial callback (as opposed to
PMCGroundings) when the number of components is one, and there is no
virtual clauses.

If we find a block is disappeared, we will increase its attention value, too.
In other case we just decrease their av.
And we will have another attention value controller to do this, and remove the new_block/disappeared predicate in each cycle.

commit message:
Add demeID in pbscored_combo_tree

In order to know from where a candidate comes from we store the
demeID (currently just the generation index) besides the combo tree
and its score. To do that the std::pair pbscored_combo_tree has been
expanded to a triplet with demeID as last element.

Note that only local_moses to supports that feature. mpi and
distributed moses store 0 and demeID. To find where to fix it search
for "@todo demeID".

commit message:
Add discriminating_bscore::full_bscore

That flag is for computing the bscores inheriting
discriminating_bscore at a finer grain.

Specifically, if enabled, the variable componant of the
discriminating_bscore is divided across all rows of the ctable. Each
one accounting for its contribution to the overall score.

This has been added to handle diversity pressure with
discriminating_bscore. By default it is disabled but once it has been
measured as yielding no overhead (which I believe) it will be enabled.

Also, only prerec_bscore currently takes advantage of it.

commit message:
Converted the libatomspace & libserver internal convenience libraries into
'real' external libraries. Additionally, I've changed the CogServer's internals
so that it is now possible to extend it. These were two direct requirements from
the Petaverse port to opencog but should help us pave the way for further
projects using the framework. I believe that as the port progresses, he'll find
a few other issues with the current opencog structure, but this should be enough
for an initial commit.

About the patch itself: there were two side-effect of turning libatomspace and
libserver into real libraries: 1) the 'src' dir was renamed to 'opencog'
(because we need to export the header files with prefixed '#include's); and 2)
the libraries are now SHARED and not STATIC.

A direct consequence of 1) is that pretty much all source files had to be
touched because I had to change all the internal opencog '#include's non-local
prefixed includes. So, '#include "AtomSpace.h"' is now '#include
<opencog/atomspace/AtomSpace.h>'.

Also, since there's now a split between framework vs client code (at least
that's what I'm trying to achieve :-)), I've chosen to move the 'examples' dir
to the root of the tree as these files are not really a part of the opencog
framework but rather client/demo applications that use it.

I also added the CMAKE directives to support "make install". To change the
install prefix, use the parameter "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:STRING=<path>":

prompt$ cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:STRING=/usr .
prompt$ make && sudo make install

Finally, to ease the task of building a project that uses the new opencog
libraries, I've added the FindOPENCOG.cmake. Any application using the opencog
framework and cmake should copy it and use it. It might be apropriate to install
this file along with the other system-wide cmake module files, but we need to
check with the cmake devs first. Also, it might be appropriate to add a
pkgconfig file so that applications have the option of using autotools instead
of cmake.

commit message:
Complete/rework diversity penalty.

Given a positive diversity pressure (from 0 to +inf), attribute each
candidate a diversity penalty determined by aggregating the diversity
penalties between that candidate and all better ones (better taking
into account their diversity_penalty). For starter, diversity is
calculated as:

diversity_pressure / (1 + Euclidean distance between bscores)

And the aggregated diversity penalty is the mean of the diversity
penalties between the candidate and the better ones.

author: Nil Geiswiller <ngeiswei@gmail.com>
commit message:
Optimize build_knobs::sample_logical_perms for feature selection within moses

When the number of feature was large (hundreds) and
build_knobs::_perm_ratio was high (around 1.0) generation of
permutations would explode even with only a feature features
selected. That code only allow to sample from permuations that are
actually permitted.

This code might be slower when the number of feature is
large (hundreds) and no feature selection occurs, but then
representation building is not scalable anyway.

Also, the previous code was sorta wrong when many features were not
permitted because it would sample amongst all features (permitted and
not) and then a probability of getting anything at all would get very
low. Here all the actual number (controlled by
build_knobs::_perm_ratio) of requested permutation is obtained.

commit message:
Apply patch from David Crane <dncrane@gmail.com> email:
[opencog-dev] list command doesn't worth properly with -T <type> -n <name>

list -t <type> -n <name> is supposed to display all atoms of a
particular type and with a particular name, and changing -t to -T is
supposed to include subtypes.

As it is now, the code assumes that there will only be one atom of a
particular type and with a particular name, which doesn't take into
account subtypes.

It also causes a segfault when the name is invalid (only when using
both -t and -n, not just -n, eg list -t ConceptNode -n <non-existent-
node-name> segfaults, but list -n <non-existent-node-name> does not)

Split eval-candidate into eval-candidate-likelihood and eval-candidate

eval-candidate-likelihood is used to compute the likelihood of a
candidate according to a certain dataset. That is the probability of
explaining that dataset.

While eval-candidate is ised to compute the score of a candidate
according to a certain fitness function (ultimately supporting the
same set than MOSES)

commit message:
add log about the diversity of the population

The log is expressed in terms of average, std, min and max distance
across all pairs of candidates in the metapopulation.

I've also replaced _cache_ddp by _cache_dst, that is it caches only
the distances between candidates rather than diversity penalty, it
shouldn't be substantially slower and that way I can cheaply extract
statistics about the distances.

author: Nil Geisweiller <ngeiswei@gmail.com>
commit message:
Modify policy of option --max-candidates so that it actually works

Select the top max candidates ignoring redundant or invalid candidates
without race condition (indeterminism).

This was the previous behavior before I replaced it with something
that would not account for redundant or invalid candidates, except it
is deterministic.

So this potentially modifies the behavior of MOSES, you might want to
lower --max-candidates to get back to similar behavior in term of
number of candidates merged.

commit message:
Work around a hang.

This should cure the hang that was seen shortly before the demo.  The
issue, not documented anywhere on github, but discussed in detail in
person and in emails, is due to the fact that a pipe fills up with print
messages from stdout, and then stalls. Since there is no python code to
drain that pipe, and the pipe is of finite size, the stall is
inevitable, as long as some, any psi-rule performs any kind of printing.

The solution here is to simply pipe all of the output to /dev/null.
This only affects the current scheme command, and anything run in it's
environment, and nothing else.

commit message:
Replace getNeighbors by get_distant_neighbors

In DefaultForwardChainerCB::choose_premises use get_distant_neighbors
instead of getNeighbors. The latter only searches neighbors via
incoming links. It turns out that some premises can be connected via
outgoing links as well. For instance given the source

InheritanceLink
    A
    B

the following premise is connected via B, an outgoing of the source

InheritanceLink
    B
    C

README was recently renamed to README.md which broke cmake config. When we run 'cmake .', we get this error:

CMake Error at /usr/share/cmake-2.8/Modules/CPack.cmake:338 (message):
  CPack package description file:

Call Stack (most recent call first):

  CMakeLists.txt:632 (INCLUDE)

To fix this, I'm editing the CmakeLists.txt so that README is replaced with README.md in cpack config.

commit message:
first round of changes towards RAM optimization of Table

Now a Table, or ITable or CTable use rows of type multi_type_seq,
which is a variant of vector<builtin>, vector<contin_t>,
vector<vertex> or vector<combo_tree>.

The first 2 (vector<builtin> and vector<contin>) are purely here to
save memory, while the last (vector<combo_tree>) is here in prevision
of using datasets with lists of functions.

commit message:
Add Scene struct inside SpaceServer to replace std::pair

It's ugly to use pair<SpaceMap, EntityManager> in the SpaceServer,
(ex. auto itr = scenes.find(maphandle);
     //we want to return SpaceMap; but this looks really confusing.
     return itr->second.first;

     //It's a little better if we can write it like this
     return itr->second.spaceMap)
We use a Scene struct to wrap them. So the SpaceServer code looks
easier to read. Note that the user of SpaceServer will not know
this wrapper.
Also fix some minor fault during this refactoring:
* make getLatestXXX return "const" reference since in the client
  code of SpaceServer we really don't use the non-const reference
  Also, the comment of getLatestXXX said that it will return const
  reference...
* replace the pointer to spaceMap and EntityRecorder with plain object
* make OctomapOcTree::clone() const method

commit message:
Implemented atomRemoved(Handle) and atomAdded(Handle) methods in AtomSpace and
connected them to AtomTable signals so that the TimeServer is always
synchronized with the AtomTable.

Fixed some issues found when testing the 'removed atom' signal:
  * Properly handle atoms removal via the 'decayShortTermImportance' method
  * AtomTable::decayShortTermImportance() returns 'void' now.
  * Unified removal of extracted handles in the removeExtractedHandles() method.
  * Inverted the order of emission of atom removal signals inside
    removeExtractedHandles() method so that removal of a Link is notified
    before the removal of the atoms in its outgoing set.

Added new tests in AtomTableUTest and AtomSpaceUTest to test the changes above.

commit message:
Make header_as<T>(key, default) behaviour consistent

Make header_as<T>(key, default) throw an exception instead of returning default
value when header value cannot be parsed properly.

                           |  Key not found | Not converted
  -------------------------+----------------+---------------
   header(key)             |     throw      |      N/A
   header(key, default)    | return default |      N/A
   header_as(key)          |     throw      |     throw
   header_as(key, default) | return default |     throw

A header record may either be missed or contain wrong data. It is error-prone
approach to ignore wrong data.

object and can be quite sure that they are correct.

Not using `add` here gives a huge performance boost because `add` gets
members each time, and then goes through them to see where the component
should fit.

commit message:
fix(helper_methods): use shallow copy

We want a copy of the object to add other inherited member_data_types_
to. If we use `=`, we get a reference to `self.member_data_types_`
object and end up modifying it, which we do not want to do. Not only
does that change the nml.py representation, it also means that all the
"expanded" lists of `member_data_types_` is held in memory for every
neuroml object which greatly increases the memory foot print of models.

So, calculate the complete list of member_data_types_ when required and
then forget about it, which will allow memory to be garbage collected
and freed up.

commit message:
feat: add method to add child/children elements to objects

- also adds a corresponding method to get some information about them

The function is added to `BaseWithoutId` and so should be inherited by
everything.

The `add` method:

- gets the list of the members defined by generateDS for each each class
- checks the type of the object being added to the types of the members
  to find the right member to add to. If a member with the type cannot
  be found, an Exception is raised.
- if a member is found, it can either be a child member (can only have
  one value) or a children member (can have multiple values in a list).
- For child members a check is made to see if a value is already set. If
  not, the value is set to the given object.
- For children members, a check is made to see if the object has already
  been added. If not, the object is added.
- If either test fails, an Exception is raised (since one does not need
  to re-add objects to update their value)
- A `force` option allows overwriting and readdition, but is set to
  `False` by default.

So, example usage would be of this type:

```
cell = neuroml.Cell(id="acell")
biprop = neuroml.BiophysicalProperties(id="biprop")
cell.add(biprop) # success
cell.add(biprop) # will throw an Exception unless `force=True`
cell.add("a string") # will throw an Exception since no member has a type "str"
```

Note: we have a few ComponentTypes which don't inherit from anywhere,
and we need to check if these are correctly defined in the XSD file
(Location is an example).

commit message:
fix: correctly fix py2/3 StringIO error

In python 2, we must use `from StringIO import StringIO` for strings.
This is not the same as `from io import StringIO` in Python2 (or in
Python3).

The former handles strings, the latter handles unicode. For Py2, since
we're not prefixing all strings with `u""` to make them unicode, we need
to use the first one.

So, different `StringIO` classes need to be imported for Python2 and
Python3. The same `from io import StringIO` cannot be shared.

- https://docs.python.org/2.7/library/stringio.html?highlight=stringio#StringIO.StringIO
- https://docs.python.org/2.7/library/io.html?highlight=io%20stringio#io.StringIO

author: Benjamin Callahan <benjamin.j.callahan@gmail.com>
commit message:
Added DETECT_SINGLETONS dadaOpt

FALSE by default, but if set to TRUE it removes the “conditional” in
the calculation of probabilties used in the core dada algorithm, which
effectively discounts the first read of any novel sequence. In
practice, this means that singletons will now be detected if they are
adjudged too unlikely to be produced under the error model, and also
increases sensitivity of detecting other low abundance sequences, i.e.
those present in just 2/3/4 reads.

In testing, this increases sensitivity to low frequency variants, but
lets a lot more junk into the final output. It is not recommended for
general purpose usage (hence the default of FALSE), but can be useful
for those who understand the high false-positive rate of singletons in
real data and want them anyway. It will also be useful as a potentially
recommended option for ultra-high-quality reads (e.g. Loop Genomics
consensus reads, and perhaps PacBio CCS in at least some circumstances)
where error rates are quire low and very well behaved.

author: benjjneb <benjamin.j.callahan@gmail.com>
commit message:
VECTORIZED_ALIGNMENT

The new vectorized aligner is now on by default
(VECTORIZED_ALIGNMENT=TRUE). This should not have any affect on the
output of dada(…). Turning the flag off reverts to the previous aligner.

The vectorized aligner uses SIMD instructions to accelerate the
computation of the Needleman-Wunsch dynamic programming matrix.

However there is an overhead cost. The vectorized aligner is about 2x
faster for the default BAND_SIZE=16, but it becomes slower for
BAND_SIZE<=8. For unbanded alignments it is about 7x faster.

author: Wojtek Bażant <wbazant@vet.upenn.edu>
commit message:
Keep stuff after the species names

The stuff after the common species name is either a number, or a strain, or whatever taxonomists put in there. I don't know how many of them would be in my data if we weren't removing them, because they all got removed :).

The change is for consideration only, do close this if you think it's a step in a worse direction.
```
> ids=c("AJ294429.1.1559 Desulfofundulus thermobenzoicus", "CP012881.1458553.1460106 Vibrio vulnificus NBRC 15645 = ATCC 27562")
> gsub("^\\S*\\s\\S*\\s", "", ids)
[1] "thermobenzoicus"                    "vulnificus NBRC 15645 = ATCC 27562"
```

Found when investigating a species of genus "Candidatus Nitrocosmicus" that got assigned to a species "Nitrocosmicus" in my data. This change won't necessarily fix it, and I have since seen that you're removing the word Candidatus from the reference as a workaround.

commit message:
Error Models

DADA now does all estimation of error rates R side. Additionally, the
user can provide the estimation function if they so wish. The function
“threepiece” is provided as a recommended default for Illumina data
with quality scores.

Error rates are now specified in 16xN matrices, with rows corresponding
to the transition (1:A->A, 2:A->C, …, 5:C->A, …) and cols correspnoding
to the average quality score from QMIN to QMAX.

When USE_QUALS=FALSE, the err matris should be 16x1.

fix(net): fix double encoding issue

The uri.setQuery() method takes an argument for whether or not to decode that was not being used.
Because of this fix, BaseServerModifier is no longer necessary (although the API for configuring it
has been left the same to avoid breaking its usage).

BREAKING CHANGE: UrlModifier now avoids doubly encoding the query string. Any steps taken on the
receiving end of these requests to code around that bug need to be reviewed and possibly removed.

BREAKING CHANGE: os.net.BaseServerExpression was removed because it was not fully featured for
parsing out domain names. Please use `new goog.Uri(str).getDomain() or `new URL(str).hostname`
instead.

commit message:
fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

author: Mike Roth <Michael.Roth@caci.com>
commit message:
feat(search): added text transform capability to search input
Added a directive and text transformers to transform input text. Transformers are registered with a manager via a plugin.
Search indexing will disregard punctuation that it doesn't recognize. Text copied from a word processing application may have smart quotes, which will be disregarded by a search analyzer while the actual intent is the treat the quoted text as a search phrase. The result is that each symbol is considered independently and the results are a union instead of being treated as a phrase. Adding the text-transform attribute to an input, and optionally, specifying a comma-separated list of transformers to text-transform-options to apply, provides a mechanism to prevent these cases by applying text transforms to the input text.

billboards no longer need the original image style off of those.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
refactor(cesium): reorganize featureconverter

This is largely a reorganization, not a rewrite or a change in logic.
FeatureConverter was a spaghetti mess and hard to make sense of for
anyone outside of a couple of experts.

The general design for the refactor is shown in sync/convertertypes.js
and sync/runconverter.js. The individual converter implementations are
all pulled in by sync/converter.js.

This is largely an attempt at feature-parity with the previous
converter, with the following changes:

  - Several style bugs were fixed by consolidating and reusing
    style code where possible instead of using the previous one-off
    implementations
  - All functions being sent a feature, geometry, style, and context now
    have a consistent parameter order everywhere
  - A few minor performance items were added (typically things like
    using scratch arrays objects where possible)
  - All instances of @suppress {checkTypes} were removed and fixed
  - Most larger functions have been split into smaller blocks with a
    couple of exceptions.

I attempted to change anything outside of FeatureConverter the least
amount possible (VectorSynchronizer and VectorContext) other than
converting them to ES6 class syntax.

FeatureConverter was previously entirely missing tests. WebGL mocks
have been added and are fleshed out engouh that we can use a real
Cesium scene in the tests. Many tests have been added but I still have
more to write.

Note that the tests currently require this PR:
https://github.com/karma-runner/karma-googmodule-preprocessor/pull/23

under a root PrimitiveCollection so that it's 'show' property can be
used to properly control their visibility.

In order to fix (many) DeveloperErrors in Cesium, lines no longer always
use the same appearance, and rather only use the
PolylineMaterialAppearance when a dash is used in the style. This allows
for better performance in general, but now we need the
isDashPatternChanging() method to check that the dashPattern is not
defined (the correct value matching the else case of no
PolylineMaterialAppearance).

commit message:
fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
refactor(cesium): reorganize featureconverter

This is largely a reorganization, not a rewrite or a change in logic.
FeatureConverter was a spaghetti mess and hard to make sense of for
anyone outside of a couple of experts.

The general design for the refactor is shown in sync/convertertypes.js
and sync/runconverter.js. The individual converter implementations are
all pulled in by sync/converter.js.

This is largely an attempt at feature-parity with the previous
converter, with the following changes:

  - Several style bugs were fixed by consolidating and reusing
    style code where possible instead of using the previous one-off
    implementations
  - All functions being sent a feature, geometry, style, and context now
    have a consistent parameter order everywhere
  - A few minor performance items were added (typically things like
    using scratch arrays objects where possible)
  - All instances of @suppress {checkTypes} were removed and fixed
  - Most larger functions have been split into smaller blocks with a
    couple of exceptions.

I attempted to change anything outside of FeatureConverter the least
amount possible (VectorSynchronizer and VectorContext) other than
converting them to ES6 class syntax.

FeatureConverter was previously entirely missing tests. WebGL mocks
have been added and are fleshed out engouh that we can use a real
Cesium scene in the tests. Many tests have been added but I still have
more to write.

Note that the tests currently require this PR:
https://github.com/karma-runner/karma-googmodule-preprocessor/pull/23

work in Windows.

Therefore, we use a well-defined path to opensphere within the
workspace.

using opensphere as a library within node_modules. That will
need to be a follow-on for later investigation.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
fix: fire event only after overridden getter ready

OL's obj.set(property, value) fires a `change:${property}` event
automatically. However, the OpenLayers event does not put the new value
on the event. Only the old value. Therefore, it is expected that a
listener for that event should be able to call the getter for that
property (in this case getSharpness or getBrightness, but also more
generically get(property)) and return the correct new value.

resolves #1046

commit message:
fix(cesium): use Image rather than ImageIcon.load

Using the underlying OL style to load the icon is problematic because
ImageIcon applies color to the image. That's all well and good, but it
requires setting the imageId in Cesium to 'src + color' rather than just
'src', which blows up the texture atlas. The solution is just to load
the image directly and let Cesium color it. The downside is that custom
extensions of those icon classes will not work properly (we do not
currently have any).

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
fix(mixin): address ng isClass failures

ng isClass() used in invoke() is incorrect in that it does not
check func.hasOwnProperty('$$ngIsClass'). If an ES6 class extends
an older class structure, isClass() will report the parent's
cached result.

Example:
  const OldClass = function() {};
  OldClass.$$ngIsClass = false;
  class NewClass extends OldClass;
  NewClass.$$ngIsClass // false!

Therefore, this mixes in a fix for that in $injector.invoke just
after os.ui.injector is set in AbstractMainCtrl.

commit message:
fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

build(windows): fix font path in Windows

The old setup was only suitable if a project had a symlink from
project/vendor/fonts to opensphere/vendor/fonts. Symlinks do not
work in Windows.

Therefore, we use a well-defined path to opensphere within the
workspace.

Note that I do not believe that this method is compatible with
using opensphere as a library within node_modules. That will
need to be a follow-on for later investigation.

commit message:
perf(cesium): improved memory usage for points

Points using RegularShape styles now (potentially) use less memory by
keeping a single instance of the shape with a white fill, using the
'color' property of the billboard to color it. I say "potentially"
because the full memory usage is still occuring on the OL/StyleManager
side when the styles are created/updated. We could potentially add a
mixin loaded by the Cesium plugin which could disable that since the
billboards no longer need the original image style off of those.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
fix: fire event only after overridden getter ready

OL's obj.set(property, value) fires a `change:${property}` event
automatically. However, the OpenLayers event does not put the new value
on the event. Only the old value. Therefore, it is expected that a
listener for that event should be able to call the getter for that
property (in this case getSharpness or getBrightness, but also more
generically get(property)) and return the correct new value.

resolves #1046

fix(kml): fix missing google maps icons

There are some google maps icons which are not available for closed
network usage by duplicating them in images/icons/kml. Previously, any
file referencing those icons failed with a message in the console and
did not show the point. This addresses that issue by checking to see if
the icon is one of the ones that we enumerate for the google icon set.

Additionally, the KML plugin now checks if maps.google.com is accessible
and sets a flag that informs whether to use the default icon for missing
URLs or just use the URL directly.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
fix(mixin): address ng isClass failures

ng isClass() used in invoke() is incorrect in that it does not
check func.hasOwnProperty('$$ngIsClass'). If an ES6 class extends
an older class structure, isClass() will report the parent's
cached result.

Example:
  const OldClass = function() {};
  OldClass.$$ngIsClass = false;
  class NewClass extends OldClass;
  NewClass.$$ngIsClass // false!

Therefore, this mixes in a fix for that in $injector.invoke just
after os.ui.injector is set in AbstractMainCtrl.

author: MarcelloNicoletti <marcello.s.nicoletti@gmail.com>
commit message:
fix(CSVExport): Prevent hidden columns from being included in export

Geometry and time fields were always included in the export, even if their
columns were hidden. This commit adds an option to always ensure a WKT geometry
field is included. This option defaults to true. When this option is false the
geometry is only included when the column is visible. This commit also changes
the time field to be included soley based on column visibility.

BREAKING CHANGE: Previously all of the following fields were always included:
`LAT`, `LON`, `LAT_DMS`, `LON_DMS`, `LAT_DDS`, `LON_DDS`, `MGRS`, `GEOMETRY`,
and `TIME`. Now only the `GEOMETRY` field is included, and it contains a WKT
representation of the data. `TIME` is now only included based on visibility.

author: MarcelloNicoletti <marcello.s.nicoletti@gmail.com>
commit message:
fix(CSVExport): Prevent hidden columns from being included in export

Geometry and time fields were always included in the export, even if their
columns were hidden. This commit adds an option to always ensure a WKT geometry
field is included. This option defaults to true. When this option is false the
geometry is only included when the column is visible. This commit also changes
the time field to be included soley based on column visibility.

BREAKING CHANGE: Previously all of the following fields were always included:
`LAT`, `LON`, `LAT_DMS`, `LON_DMS`, `LAT_DDS`, `LON_DDS`, `MGRS`, `GEOMETRY`,
and `TIME`. Now only the `GEOMETRY` field is included, and it contains a WKT
representation of the data. `TIME` is now only included based on visibility.

commit message:
fix(cesium): hacky fix for some bugs in Cesium's explicit rendering

The old ol-cesium render loop fired rendering when Cesium's request
stack finished a request. This has been restored. Additionally,
when the render loop is fired via a GL_REPAINT event, the loop
continuously renders for a whole second at the target framerate
rather than simply rendering once. This covers the async load of
an icon and asynchronously loading it to the GPU.

THIN-11821

commit message:
fix(net): credentials handler should not save results

Some servers provide error pages that are redirected and do not result in error code responses
(maintenance pages are also occasionally a problem if they do not return 503). Therefore,
CredentialsHandler should not save information because it can't really know if the request "worked"
outside of the status code.

commit message:
fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

commit message:
fix(cesium): fix collection visibility

Cesium prefers wide scene trees to deep ones, but there are several
collection implementations that do not implement the 'show' property,
preventing us from setting the visibility at the collection level
(representing layer visibility). Therefore, these collections are added
under a root PrimitiveCollection so that it's 'show' property can be
used to properly control their visibility.

did not show the point. This addresses that issue by checking to see if

and sets a flag that informs whether to use the default icon for missing
URLs or just use the URL directly.

commit message:
fix(cesium): use dash change detection

In order to fix (many) DeveloperErrors in Cesium, lines no longer always
use the same appearance, and rather only use the
PolylineMaterialAppearance when a dash is used in the style. This allows
for better performance in general, but now we need the
isDashPatternChanging() method to check that the dashPattern is not
defined (the correct value matching the else case of no
PolylineMaterialAppearance).

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
commit message:
fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

ImageIcon applies color to the image. That's all well and good, but it
requires setting the imageId in Cesium to 'src + color' rather than just
'src', which blows up the texture atlas. The solution is just to load
the image directly and let Cesium color it. The downside is that custom
extensions of those icon classes will not work properly (we do not
currently have any).
